steps.name: Yura
steps.text: No, can't write that.

steps.name: Yura
steps.text: 'Cleanse the gray streets with snow water'? 'Bring a wet pack of smokes'? No, that's not right either!
By the pale moonlight he gazes upon the heavily-marked draft, lamenting his lack of inspiration. This poem was worse than his fellow student's sleep-talking on the bunk next to him.
The Unbound camp is eerily quiet after the fire, the winter wind like a blunt knife cutting upon the young people's faces.
The ones that still have strength left whisper to each other, wrapping themselves in moldy jackets, looking like mounds of dirt under the dark night, occasionally laughing softly.

steps.name: Yura
steps.text: ...Give every star a name to remember.

steps.name: Yura
steps.text: Give those who want to forget a cup of cheap spirits.

steps.name: Yura
steps.text: Give me...

steps.name: Yura
steps.text: Give me a one-way ticket to spring...

steps.name: Yura
steps.text: Let me live in the wind that blows upon the tundra.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Boo—

steps.name: Yura
steps.text: You again... I swear, one of these days, I'll be immune to your pranks.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: You're writing those stupid poems again, Yura.

steps.name: Yura
steps.text: They are not stupid poems! I put my heart and soul in them. Besides, you can't even read them.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Don't want to. People who can read, people like you, always have such sullen looks on your faces.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Matvey's taught me how to read addresses. At the end of the day, whatever you guys are writing, I'm the one who has to deliver it for you.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Say it, Yura. Which girl am I delivering to this time?

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Ouch—

steps.name: Yura
steps.text: This is for you, little brat!

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: You hit me! I'm taking this away so that you don't get to write it!

steps.name: Yura
steps.text: Come on, it's just a roll of paper, it can't have hurt all that much... but you can have it, if you want.

steps.name: Yura
steps.text: This time... I'm writing for everyone. Including you.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: You're so weird... I'll put it in my bag, then.

steps.name: Yura
steps.text: Never mind that, Ukusik.

steps.name: Yura
steps.text: You should talk to Antosha. I think he has a lot of letters there.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Doesn't he eat and spend the nights with you guys? Why don't I see him around?

steps.name: Yura
steps.text: Who knows? He's in there. Ask him for me.

steps.name: Yura
steps.text: And pull that jacket tighter. He'll yell at us if you catch a cold.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Hm? He never yells at me.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Bye, Yura.

steps.name: Yura
steps.text: That's because we are the ones he yells at, little brat...

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: I'm here, Antosha.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: No need to be so loud every time, Ukusik.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Yura said you've got letters to give to me. Where?

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Yes. There's quite a lot.
He goes to the corner and picks up a thick stack of letters.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Oh, bother... lemme see.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: This one's for No. 34 Odoyev Old Street? The second is No. 15 Zheleznaya Left Bank Street, the third one to the spice market...

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Wait, did you write all these letters, Antosha? What are these places?

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: No. 34 Odoyev Old Street is Yura's home, then Lev's and Vissarion's...

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: I wrote one for everyone. We'll see how many you'll need to deliver after we take that magistrate down.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: If any fall tomorrow... I don't want their families to learn about them from casualty reports.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: When did you memorize all this?

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: When someone entrusts their life to me, I must know where it comes from... I can never forget it.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: You remember how I asked where you came from?

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: You just didn't expect me to be an orphan with no name.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Hey, what's that look on your face?

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: I've never been as depressed as you look, and I'm the one who had no parents and no name. Besides, I saved you a piece of paper.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Say, are you and Matvey's letters in this pile too?

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: Mine, perhaps, but certainly not his.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Matvey?

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: We usually meet before we do something big.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Do you have beer?

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: Last two bottles. Someone stuffed them under a pile of rotten vegetables, but List sniffed them out while we were preparing equipment.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: ...Give me one.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Can I try? I'm thirsty—

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: How old do you think you are? Forget it.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Zhopa!
Matvey pats her on the head, then sits beside Antosha and gives him a bottle.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Why did you say Antosha won't write home?

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Why does he have me deliver letters if he thinks he won't die? Is he scared?

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: Hah, of course not...

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: He hasn't had any contact with his family for a long time.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: Antosha?

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: It's alright. All in the past now.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: The subject of Antosha came up in a conversation with someone else, not long after we met.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: I accidentally called him Anton Shestov, which he happened to overhear. He was in a sullen mood for a month afterwards.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Anton Shestov? Sounds like some important noble.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: I abandoned the name and the one who gave it to me before I went to university.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: I expect they're more relieved to be rid of a troublemaking traitor than saddened by the loss of a son.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: I've never heard about Antosha's family before...

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Were they mean to you?

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: My grandfather killed the landlord who oppressed him and returned home a count.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: He was the 'hero' that I wanted to grow up to be, so I imitated the stories, ate and lived with the serfs, and made friends with all the peasant servants.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: I didn't care that my family didn't think it was proper. I thought that at least my grandfather would understand.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Until I grew older and wiser...

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: When an old serf accidentally knocked him over, my grandfather forced the man to strangle the pet musbeast he had raised for years with his own hands, right in front of us.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: Antosha, you don't have to talk about this—

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Still, I continued to fantasize... until that night when my grandfather held a great feast to celebrate my acceptance into a Grypherburg university.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: A maid around the same age as me sneaked into the kitchen and took some food, hoping to give her mother and brother a treat.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: The police wanted to take her, but my grandfather stopped them.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: He said with a laugh, 'Today is a good day. I want everyone to be happy for my grandson's glory.'

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: A couple of days later, I saw a body by the side of the road as I was traveling to Grypherburg. There were bloody whip marks all over her.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: The butler told me that the police would only keep her in jail for a few days. Only the noble right of corporal punishment could 'teach her a real lesson'.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: But it was I who learned the lesson. I see the flies crawling over her eyelashes whenever I close my eyes.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: That was when I learned that oppression will persist as long as the nobility does, as long as the only outcome of any struggle is to turn different people into nobles.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Let me tell you this, Antosha.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: The worst has already passed... we'll win.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Tomorrow, by tomorrow, I—
She slurs the last few words and passes out on Matvey's shoulder.
With a start, Antosha snatches the bottle from Ukusik's arms. It is completely empty.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Ukusik—and I was wondering how you learned to comfort a man like that.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: You stole my booze... why didn't you watch her, Matvey?

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: For the better, I suppose... don't wake her. I was just thinking about how to get her to leave.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: It's time to take her away.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: But you know that where we're going...

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Heh...

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: I'll help.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: So... did you write a letter for me too?

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: There's no need. I trust you.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: I had Ukusik take a letter to my mother a little while back, when she could still get out through the hole.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: What did you write?

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: 'We'll be out of this place and back in the city in ten days, at most.'

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: It's time to go, my friend.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Remember to come back.
Matvey closes his eyes and nods.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Good night, Matvey...

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: See you at dawn.

steps.name: Excited Student
steps.text: How long is it gonna take, Rosalind? You've been fiddling with that all night.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: It's a guitar, not some rag doll.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: You dug this out of the trash heap without a single working peg. No way to fix this fast.

steps.name: Excited Student
steps.text: Well, tomorrow's the big day. We'll take all the notes you can give us.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Hmph... give me the clamps.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: ...Have you checked everything?

steps.name: Cautious Student
steps.text: Yes. The building is structurally sound. The wounded will be safe there.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Good. Talk to Mykola and double-check the assignments on both sides of the street.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: No mistakes, you understand?

steps.name: Cautious Student
steps.text: Yes, ma'am!
...Bad timing, Sonya?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Matvey?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: What are you doing here? Did something happen on your side? Anything we can do?

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: Thanks, but we're fine.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: The way Antosha was talking back there... he wouldn't come to you even if he was starving to death, that stubborn hard-head.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: I came because of her.
He turns sideways and shows the snoring girl behind him.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: She smells of...

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: She got into the beer while we weren't looking.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: I want to give her to you. Given the manpower and battle plans, she'll be safer with your group.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Rosalind still has a few mats. Go and talk to her.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: Thank you. I mean it.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: I was afraid that after your argument...

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: He may be ice cold... but we have to admit you are all great warriors.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: ...Antosha used to be more passionate.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: He was a strange one from the day I met him. He had the demeanor of a great noble, but he kept pestering our teacher about where he could pick up odd jobs.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: He assisted the professor in writing essays that criticized aristocratic politics. The council at the time did not punish them; they even promoted the professor to school inspector.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: That day, Antosha took my hands and said there was hope for Ursus at least. People will no longer suffer, and we will all be free.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: We planted a cherry tree in the school garden to celebrate the occasion.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: Until our newspaper was shut down, and the professor died for us...

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: We were expelled. The professor shouldered most of the responsibility in exchange for an 'amnesty' towards us.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: The night before we left school, Antosha sat in front of the cherry tree, stroking its leafless branches. He sat there all night.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: I should find Rosalind. Thank you again.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: One moment, Matvey.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: You said it was safer to stay here...

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Why don't you stay?

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: No, I made a promise tonight.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: ...Or long before that, perhaps.

steps.name: Excited Student
steps.text: Did it work?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Let me try.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Not quite in tune, but at least it makes a sound now.

steps.name: Excited Student
steps.text: Yay! I knew you were a genius, Rosalind!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: NOW you try to sweet-talk me. How about you spend that time thinking what you want to hear?

steps.name: Excited Student
steps.text: Okay... 'On the Old River'? Or some Leithanian song...

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Hmph, I'm not playing that soft sentimental stuff.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: How about I improvise a few chords, and you guys sing something that fits the scene?

steps.name: Excited Student
steps.text: Isn't that a bit hard?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: What did you take all those literature courses for? Start thinking about the lyrics, because here I go.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: One, two, three...
Step over cobwebs of iron♪
Strip the night's hard shell♪
Come, brothers and sisters♪
The spring sprout will break through the frozen soil♪
Instead of waiting for a false dawn in the snow♪

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Mm... this sound...

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: ...Matvey?

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Still no news?

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: How much time do you think has already passed?!

steps.name: Security Team Captain
steps.text: We've secured the sentry turrets on the two roads, but—

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Was I asking about the turrets? I'm talking about reinforcements and supplies!

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: What about the crossbows that Daniila Treplev promised me? What about the artillery? The tanks? The armies?

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: I sent him a thousand letters, and he hasn't written a single word back!

steps.name: Security Team Captain
steps.text: Please, calm down, sir. The few of us here are well-equipped with crossbows and emergency catapult systems. We can assure your safety.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: 'Calm down'? 'The few of us'?

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Are you telling me that I hired you so that I can pay your wages? You think they'll just let me go if I run away? How's that any different from being dead?

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: If you want your money, 'captain', you'd better do your jobs and kill those troublemakers!

steps.name: Security Team Captain
steps.text: But you only had the budget for the few of us, some of whom you sent to help Gromov, while there are hundreds of them—

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: I don't need you to tell me! I can hear them singing through my window!

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: They're singing my elegy!

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: ...Who are you?

steps.name: Ursine Officer
steps.text: Good evening, magistrate. I am Captain Chicherin.

steps.name: Ursine Officer
steps.text: You must have plenty of supplies here, to turn the heat up so high that you are sweating so much.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: You... no, no. You bring help from Duke Treplev? Please, take a seat.

steps.name: Ursine Officer
steps.text: No, His Grace is no longer interested in Katorga Raion.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Why?!

steps.name: Ursine Officer
steps.text: It is not my place to guess at His Grace's intentions.

steps.name: Ursine Officer
steps.text: However, while he did not send me, it is true that I am here to support you.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Yes... I knew the empire would reward my loyalty for my service in Katorga.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: How many men do you have? How many heavy weapons? You can set them up at once. Put a cannon in this room, for all I care!

steps.name: Ursine Officer
steps.text: I'm afraid you misunderstood.

steps.name: Ursine Officer
steps.text: I do not have men. My superior assigned me thirty guards, and no heavy weapons.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: What?!

steps.name: Ursine Officer
steps.text: However, he has prepared this for you.
The officer takes out a black, palm-sized box and hands it to Pavlovich.

steps.name: Ursine Officer
steps.text: It is an encrypted military terminal connected directly to an artillery position outside the city.

steps.name: Ursine Officer
steps.text: If you are truly desperate... press the red button, and we will provide 'suitable' firepower coverage.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: What do you mean by 'suitable'? I want to level the whole district.

steps.name: Ursine Officer
steps.text: That would be impossible. Every shell has a cost, and every block is an asset, even in Katorga Raion.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: What about Originium bolts? Explosives? Surely you could carry those?

steps.name: Ursine Officer
steps.text: All here.
Only then does Pavlovich notice that the officer is carrying two small briefcases.

steps.name: Ursine Officer
steps.text: This is to avoid the weapons falling into the hands of the rioters. After all, the supplies that were given to you have been taken by the students. We can only risk so much.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: I... I did your dirty work, and you people just...

steps.name: Ursine Officer
steps.text: Your sponsors have shown plenty of good will by putting thirty elite men at your disposal.

steps.name: Ursine Officer
steps.text: Besides, I believe you underestimate the 'weapon' in your hands. Press it, and Ursus will bestow upon you the supreme 'glory'...
The magistrate ponders the meaning of these words as he clutches the cold communicator in his sweaty palm.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Yes... I cannot abandon hope... they will help me, I can beat that rabble...

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Guards!

steps.name: 'Sixteen Warriors' Thug
steps.text: You called, sir?

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: How many of you are still combat-ready?

steps.name: 'Sixteen Warriors' Thug
steps.text: Three to four hundred, I think?

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: As long as it's more than the other side. Get them warmed up. I'll give them their revenge for Gromov!

steps.name: 'Sixteen Warriors' Thug
steps.text: Aye, sir!

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: You, plant explosives at the door. If they dare to come in, we'll all go and see Igor Velikiy together!

steps.name: Security Team Captain
steps.text: Uh...

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: As for you, Captain, I need you to deal with the Unbound.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Do not underestimate them. I've been fighting them for two months. They are few in number, but they are experienced.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: More importantly, they kill any nobles they see on sight... harbor no fantasies about them. The council would not want to let them out.

steps.name: Ursine Officer
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Ursine Officer
steps.text: If my ears do not deceive me... someone is coming.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: ...Let's go.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: It's time to teach these brats a lesson.
